name: Pamp

attributes.attribute: name may derive from the Latin Pompeius

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Pamp is an Irish hero. The Book of Invasions also calls him Pam. The book names him as the father of Nemed. This made Pamp an ancestor of the Nemedians. The Nemedians were among the early invaders of Ireland. Scholars believe his name is a late invention. It may derive from the Latin name Pompeius.

okr.objective: Describe Pamp, an Irish hero and ancestor of the Nemedians.
key_results: The Book of Invasions names Pamp as the father of Nemed.
He was an ancestor of the Nemedian invaders of Ireland.
His name may come from the Latin name Pompeius.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
